root_cause.text: Missing cleanup of access_pattern subdirectories in the error path of `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs()` when scheme directory setup fails after access_pattern/ directory creation, leaving dangling sysfs entries and causing memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a call to `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(scheme->access_pattern)` before the existing `kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj)` in the error label `rmdir_put_access_pattern_out`, and the CVE description explicitly states that subdirectories of access_pattern/ are not cleaned up on failure, leading to broken sysfs interface and memory leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incomplete cleanup in error path of DAMON sysfs scheme creation to avoid stale directories.
intent_record.what: Changed the goto label in error handling from `put_access_pattern_out` to `rmdir_put_access_pattern_out` when `damos_sysfs_set_dests` fails in `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs`.
intent_record.how: Previously, a failure in `damos_sysfs_set_dests` would skip cleaning up the previously created sysfs directory structure, potentially leaving stale entries. Now the function jumps to a label that performs the required cleanup (removing the directory) before putting the access pattern.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing cleanup of access pattern sysfs directories in the error path of damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs.
intent_record.what: Renamed the label `put_access_pattern_out` to `rmdir_put_access_pattern_out` and added a call to `damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs(scheme->access_pattern)` before the existing `kobject_put` and NULL assignment.
intent_record.how: In the error/cleanup path of `damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs`, the new code now removes the sysfs directories for the access pattern prior to decrementing the kobject reference count, ensuring proper cleanup of sysfs entries.

bic_trace_step.reason: In damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs, after creating access_pattern and its subdirectories via damon_sysfs_scheme_set_access_pattern, subsequent failures (e.g., in damos_sysfs_set_dests or damon_sysfs_scheme_set_quotas) lead to the error path that only does kobject_put(&scheme->access_pattern->kobj) at 'put_access_pattern_out'. It does not call damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs to clean up the subdirectories (weights, ranges) created under access_pattern, causing dangling sysfs entries and memory leak. This vulnerability is present and not fixed in this commit.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:

Author: SeongJae Park <sj@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Oct 26 22:59:41 2022 +0000

    mm/damon/sysfs: split out schemes directory implementation to separate file
    
    DAMON sysfs interface for 'schemes' directory is implemented using about
    one thousand lines of code.  It has no strong dependency with other
    parts of its file, so split it out to another file for better code
    management.
    
    Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/202210262259
bic_trace_step.reason: The function damon_sysfs_scheme_add_dirs() (lines ~709-734) has an error path that only performs kobject_put on the access_pattern kobject without first cleaning up its subdirectories (sz, nr_accesses, age). In case of failure after successful creation of the access_pattern directory and its subdirectories, the subdirectories are left dangling, causing memory leak and leftover sysfs entries. The cleanup for access_pattern subdirectories (damon_sysfs_access_pattern_rm_dirs) is not called on error; only kobject_put is used, which does not remove the children. This matches the root cause.
